exposure: Speckle tracking analysis (RV and LV area, lengths, widths, sphericity indices, contractility)
outcome: Urgent neonatal balloon atrial septostomy (BAS) requirement
cohort: The study participants were 39 fetuses diagnosed with D-Transposition of the great arteries (D-TGA) and intact ventricular septum.
finding: Speckle tracking analysis identified measurable differences in RV and LV size, shape, and contractility between fetuses who underwent neonatal urgent BAS and those who did not, effectively predicting 91% of neonates requiring the procedure.
